questions.q: Q70. List 6 on-site resources provided by a Major Hazard Facility?
a: Booster Connections – Static Water Supply
Tactical Fire Plans, Floor Plans
Shutting off – rerouting of supplies
Ring mains water/foam
Installed monitors
Foam/dry chem
Deluge
Onsite Bunding and drain isolation valves
Spill kits
Specialist advice

questions.q: Q71. What must you always have with you at an Electrical Sub Station fire?
questions.a: Firefighter shall not enter unless accompanied by an electrical supply company representative or other trainer / authorised person.

questions.q: Q72. List your actions when on scene at a Pole fire? (6)
a: Request Electrical Company attend
No attempt to extinguish the fire until electrical company has confirmed the area has been made electrically safe
Protect exposure if required
Only attack fire if absolutely necessary for preservation of life:
Using PARTIAL FOG or BROKEN STREAM – Do NOT use Jet
Avoid hitting wires directly with water
Spraying stream above pole and lob onto fire
Not standing in pools of water or wet surfaces

questions.q: Q73. Electrical Substation Actions:
a: Fire/Incident – No rescue
Respond electrical supply company
Protect exposures
Keep firefighters clear
No water jets

questions.q: Q74. List your actions when attending premises that have or may have Uninterrupted Power Supplies, as stated in the ERG (4):
a: UPS may be present when dealing with computers, telephone exchanges, process controllers
Treat all such equipment as live
Isolate power between electrical equipment and UPS
Consider requesting electrical company to ensure power isolation

questions.q: Q75. Aerial Appliances Considerations:
a: Always use a spotter when working near powerlines
3 Meters from powerline – No Go Zone

questions.q: Q76. What are the on-scene considerations for FIA?
a: Obstacles preventing entry into the building
Extent of the fire on arrival
Location / intensity / colour of flames/smoke
Indications of forcible entry
Condition of doors/windows (covered/broken)

questions.q: Q77. List the criteria for response of fire investigators Request of Commander or above:
a: Undetermined structure fires
Bushfires within FRV's jurisdiction
All fire related deaths
All fire related serious injuries
Any fire related firefighter injury
Fires involving FRV property
At the request of a Commander or above

questions.q: Q78. What are the Properties of LPG?
a: UN number of LPG, 1075
Hazchem 2YE
Expansion Ratio: 270:1
LEL 1.5%, UEL 10%
Heavier than air
Cylinders silver, bullets white

questions.q: Q79. List 6 actions to be implemented when attending calls to Hospitals as outlined in the FERG. (12 all up):
a: Identify the Emergency Co-Ordinator / Chief Warden / Security
Locate and Access EIC
Check SDS
PA Colour Code Announcement
Confine incident
Assist Evacuation (Ambulant, Semi-Ambulant, Non-Ambulant)
Ambulance - Request additional AV Units
Check Operating Theatre progress
Isolate Medical Gases
Check Staffing / Patient Levels
Check High Security Patients
Check plant room / vent systems

questions.q: Q80. When at a hybrid vehicle incident, how long is power maintained for in the SRS system?
Q81. When at a hybrid vehicle incident, how do you immobilise the car and remove the HEV fuse, if the correct fuse cannot be recognized?
questions.a: Remove the Yellow (20 amp). If unable to identify correct fuse, remove all.

questions.q: Q82. When at a hybrid vehicle incident, how long is power maintained for in the high voltage electrical system?
Q83. Removing the key from a hybrid vehicle and put it in a safe location after an incident. How many metres must you place it away from the vehicle?
Q84. You are first on-scene at a car fire involving LPG. List your "Actions" during the fire:
a: Utilise hose line from sheltered position
Cool cylinder by directing flooding quantities of water onto upper surfaces until well after fire is out
Use dry chemical, Carbon Dioxide, or water spray to extinguish fire

questions.q: Q85. You are first on scene at a car fire involving LPG. List your "Actions" after the fire:
a: Cool the tank with water spray
Consider flare-off remaining contents (gas flare off kit on heavy rescue vehicles)
Apply damaged cylinder sticker on cylinder
Advise the owner to have cylinder tested

questions.q: Q86. You are dispatched to a car fire involving LPG. List 4 safety actions only if safe to do so:
a: Disconnect the battery under water spray
Open the boot under water spray
Locate the tank to find liquid service valve
Isolate the gas by shutting liquid service valve

questions.q: Q87. LPG CAR FIRE – SAFETY:
a: Do not extinguish burning gas if tank is still venting; leave to burn
Beware of an increase in fire intensity/pitch of escaping gas – indications of the situation deteriorating and risk of tank failure/rupture
Evacuate if tank is suspected of rupturing
Do not direct water at venting pressure relief valve as icing may occur

questions.q: Q88. What are the considerations at a Car Fire?
a: Availability of water supply – respond water tanker or pumper tanker if required
Fuel source (petrol, diesel, LPG, hybrid, hydrogen powered, compressed natural gas powered and alternative fuel sources)
Undeployed airbags (including side intrusion / curtain)
Be aware once 12 volt battery is disconnected, the handbrakes may not engage / disengage, it may be impossible to open the boot, open or close windows, etc.

questions.q: Q89. What are CityLink Fire/Hazmat Considerations?
a: Confirm location of fire from CityLink Traffic Control Room and ensure the effected tunnel is closed to traffic
Consider use of installed telephone systems in tunnels
Evacuate tunnel as required via emergency access points or use safe havens within tunnel
Respond VicPol to assist evacuation
Within the tunnels:
The IC shall make every effort to contain pollutants to the incident site however during major incidents pollutants can be permitted into drains
Minor Hazmat and biohazard incidents should be managed at road surface level only
On the open roads:
All pollutants must be managed at road level
The IC is to consider 'bunding' of the drains or applying absorbent, etc.

questions.q: Q90. What are the Minor hazardous incidents/petrol washaways Actions for CityLink?
a: Confirm the location of the incident, request and confirm a lane closure adjacent to location of incident from the CityLink TCR (or a requirement to close the tunnel)
Control of pollutants in the tunnels and open roadways as above
DO NOT use sand
Check hydrocarbon alarms installed in underground pit and above filtration tanks and if operated, flush the drainage system until the alarm resets

questions.q: Q91. Rubbish tips and waste sites, who to notify?
a: Council MERO
EPA
Department of Health, if required
Workcover
Operations Commander
Fire Safety Issue Notification

questions.q: Q92. What are your actions when responded to a prison (secured facility) incident/fire?
a: Meet with the Facility Liaison Officer (LO) and Field Commander (FC) at entrance to site
The attending OIC is to ascertain nature and status of event, status of secured facility and assess situation
Enter only on request of facility management, if site security is confirmed, and only under the guidance of an escort / liaison officer – one per appliance
If requested to enter and is deemed safe to do so, and if the need arises the IC is to notify MFB Operations Commander of CFA Rostered Duty Officer
Fire service personnel to receive briefing from facility staff including arrangements for any emergency evacuation plan
A Minimum number of appliances and crew will be committed, IC to determine
Routine security checks undertaken in consideration of situation
Fire services to Withdraw if safety/crew threatened

questions.q: Q93. List Considerations at a high-rise building:
a: As for low rise plus
Evacuation (floor and roof area)
Falling debris perimeter
Tactical fire plans, floor plans, MSDS
Comms plan – consider alternative trunked channel
Sectors – floor or level number
Use of firefighters lift (manned)
Refuge zones
Ultra-high rise >55 levels – check for fire pumps on upper levels are operating, if not, use Rosenbauer
Ensure clearance for ULP is provided
Building class, contents, fire load
Industry type
Dangerous goods
Location, severity, behaviour of fire
Specialist advice/services
Sprinklers/fire protection systems
Boosting ring mains, hydrants, sprinklers
Static water supply, foam, hose reels
Smoke management – air handling
Wardens
Evac points/BA service/Staging area, BA entry
Sectors 1,2,3,4
Community warnings
Aerial/specialist appliances (siting)
Salvage/ventilation
Rehab/fire duty
FIA/ fire safety
After the fire pamphlets
Firefighter welfare, CIS
Business continuity
USAR/HART

questions.q: Q94. When safe working at heights procedures is being employed. List four considerations:
a: Respond HART
Possibly use Aerial appliances
Separate radio channel
TIC

questions.q: Q95. Actions – Ports and Docks, as stated in the FERG:
a: Liaise with Port Authority Personnel
Seek specialist advice
Maintain flashing lights at all times
Be aware of other vehicles in dock areas

questions.q: Q96. Safety Docks & Ports:
a: Beware of load limitations on piers, jetties, and wharves. No vehicles are to be driven onto these that do not have a weight limitation plaque
Exercise caution when parking near edges
PFD worn when working within 2 meters of body of water
Caution, establish a 2 meter safety zone around edges
Appoint a safety officer when working near water

questions.q: Q97. Considerations – Ports and Docks, as stated in the FERG:
a: Waterway Emergency Response operators
Beware of weight limitations/loading on wharves and appliance exclusion zones
Do not enter if load limit is not identified. Marine response for safety, lighting, firefighting, booms, and specialist advice

Tugs – available if required for firefighting west of Bolte Bridge only. SF1s to be assigned to operate water monitors on tugs. The tug Coxswain has overriding responsibility for the safety of the vessel and the crew

Shipping container – obtain container number (2, 3 or 4 alpha characters, followed by 6-7 numeric characters e.g., CRXU2933507) and relay to Comm Centre for details of contents. Number marked on all sides of container

questions.q: Q98. What are the actions required when dispatched to a ship fire?
a: Respond fire boat (FRV) / Respond Coast Guard (CFA)
Establish & Maintain contact Ships SENIOR OFFICER on board
Report to THE SHIPS BRIDGE
Determine LOCATION AND ACCESS to fire and INTENSITY
Access INFORMATION:
SHIPS PLANS
Firefighting ALREADY UNDERTAKEN
Operation of FIREFIGHTING INSTALLATIONS / EQUIPMENT
Details of CARGO / MANIFEST / LOG
State of SHIPS SERVICES power, water
VENTILATION
Ship's STABILITY
State of the ships HATCHES
Fire service vessels or fire tugs to Cool exterior of the vessel
MONITOR AMOUNT of water used/removal of FIREFIGHTING WATER
Establish ORIGIN OF IGNITION
Consider/monitor ALTERNATIVE EXTINGUISHING media

questions.q: Q99. What are your considerations for inland waterway pollution control?
a: Size, location, and type of spill
Identify control agency
Specialist advice early on
Accessing State cache of equipment
Waterway Emergency Responder (WER) response

questions.q: Q100. List your considerations when attending incidents involving Trams (4):
a: Trams operate on 600 volt DC tractive control from overhead trolley wire
Power control centre is able to isolate power to each section in the network remotely. However isolation is not ensured until maintenance crews confirm on site
Responding Heavy Rescue pod (MFB)
Responding High Angle Rescue if incident involves roof of tram

questions.q: Q101. Victoria Police – Municipal Emergency Response Coordinator (MERC):
questions.a: VicPol District Senior Sergeant (MERC) has the responsibility to coordinate requests from the Fire Service, including but not limited to accommodation, logistics, support resources or issues related to recovery activities. The MERC should be embedded into the EMT at the earliest convenience, regardless of the size of the incident.

questions.q: Q102. Bomb threat siting?
Q103. What are your actions at a Bomb threat in the appliance?
a: Utilise open space where possible
Park appliance facing away
Appliance location to – Notify Comms Centre or location
ALL FF in rear seat windows open
Maintain clear access and egress at all times

questions.q: Q104. List your actions for FRV first on-scene or present at time of event Hostile Act (3):
a: Immediately withdraw to a safe location and send signal 5 5 to Firecom detailing circumstances of the hostile act
Firecom will request immediate attendance of Victoria Police and send notifications to ensure high level situational awareness and organisational readiness
Restrict Access to the area

questions.q: Q105. Appliance Siting Considerations for Hostile Acts/Bomb Threats:
a: Park minimum 300 meter from area until the incident site has been assessed by Bomb Response Unit personnel (BRU)
Utilise open space wherever possible
Park appliance facing away
Notify Comm Centre of location of appliances
All firefighters stay in rear seat, side windows open
Maintain clear access and egress all times

questions.q: Q106. Air wing authorisation/guidelines:
questions.a: Requests for Victorian Police air support in emergency situations may be made through the on-scene VicPol coordinator.

questions.q: Q107. Responsibilities of the Incident Controller:
a: Take control of all resources at fires/incidents
Assume responsibility for the health, safety, and actions of all responding personnel at that fire/incident at all times
Ensure all OICs of appliances report to the Incident Control Point for tasking
Conduct an initial incident Size Up and continue throughout the incident
Develop and implement an Incident Action Plan (IAP)
Implement an Incident Management System
Establish Incident Emergency Management Teams (IEMT)
Initiate Community Information/Warning messages as required
Provide regular Situation Reports for FRV senior command
Establish a Communications Plan
Manage and track resources
Document/log pertinent incident information
Transfer control where required
Determine the cause of the fire, where possible
Assist in organising emergency accommodation for displaced persons where required
Notify Local Government Area if concerned about potential for residents to remain in uninhabitable fire affected properties
Conduct an appropriate After Action Review

questions.q: Q108. Name two Actions for Establishing Incident Control Points:
a: Establish an Incident Control Point at every fire/incident. This is the responsibility of the OIC of the first arriving appliance
Name each Incident Control Point and communicate the name to the Communications Centre

questions.q: Q109. List your considerations for establishing a control point (OMS 001):
a: Establish an Incident Control Point at every fire/incident. This is the responsibility of the OIC of the first arriving appliance
Name each Incident Control Point and communicate the name to the Communications Centre
Establish an Incident Control Point, taking the following into consideration:
Ease of access
Prominence of location with a good overview of the incident
Ability to stage and deploy all arriving appliances and support agency personnel
Safety from any incident hazards
Potential impediments to incident communications
Ensure the Incident Controller wears a tabard

questions.q: Q110. List 3 Examples of When Sectors Should be Established:
a: Establish incident sectors with appointed Sector Commanders at incidents where the scale and complexity is likely to limit the Incident Controller's situational awareness, particularly where:
Operations are taking place in more than one location, or remotely from the Incident Control Point
The span of control on the fireground exceeds 1:5
Technical operations are taking place

questions.q: Q111. Sector Commander roles and responsibilities:
a: Obtain a SMEACSQ briefing from the Operations Officer or Incident Controller

Implement the section of the Incident Action Plan relevant to the sector, with consideration to RECEO and the Emergency Management Priorities published in the Victorian State Emergency Management Plan
Brief all personnel allocated to the sector
Allocate tasks to resources within the sector and maintain control of the resources
Implement and monitor safety and welfare measures of all personnel within the sector
Conduct regular Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessments (SPADRA) and perform continual Size Up for the duration of the shift
Provide regular strategic level Situation Reports through the chain of command
Wear a tabard to identify the role
Ensure the allocated crews work within the established Communications Plan and monitor the effectiveness of communications
Work with the Safety Officer appointed to the sector
Ensure Rapid Intervention Teams (RIT) are formed where required and located in a ready status at appropriate locations for the sector
Coordinate activities with adjoining sectors
Respond additional resources for the sector via the chain of command when necessary
Report all accidents, injuries, hazards or near misses through the chain of command
Resolve problems as they arise
Participate in development of plans for the next operational period
Maintain a log of all activities

questions.q: Q112. Who Establishes the Creation and Location of Incident Sectors?
Q113. Incident Sectors – Actions – 6 General Requirements:
a: Establish incident sectors with appointed Sector Commanders at incidents where the scale and complexity is likely to limit the Incident Controller's situational awareness
Ensure the creation and location of incident sectors is only established under instruction from the Incident Controller
Allocate appropriately ranked and experienced personnel to the role of Sector Commander where available
Appoint a Safety Officer to all sectors where resources permit
Ensure all crews and appliances report directly to the Sector Commander for tasking
Consider conducting Atmospheric Monitoring at designated Sector Command Points

questions.q: Q114. What are the 4 Sectors at an incident?
Q115. List all of the High-Rise Sectors:
a: Fire Sector
Operations Point
Lobby Sector
Evacuation Sector

questions.q: Q116. Objectives of Incident Action Plan:
a: Include a statement of intent within incident objectives, adhering to the SMART principle:
Specific – Language and actions stated can be easily communicated and understood
Measurable – Specific actions and timeframes are stated so progress and completion of the objective can be evaluated
Achievable – Selected strategies and tactics are realistic considering resource availability and identified risks/hazards
Relevant – Objective includes consideration of Size Up information, State Emergency Management Plan, and identified risks/hazards
Time frame – Specific time anticipated to achieve objective
Consider implementing recovery efforts during the response phase of an incident to enable possible early rehabilitation activities, business continuity, and lessen other community impacts

questions.q: Q117. When En Route Consider the following for Size Up:
a: Any existing pre-plans or Site Specific Risk Information (e.g., flammable cladding, height of structure, hoarding, criminal activity, fuel load, dangerous animals)
Alarmed premises with keys held on station
Any further information provided from the Communications Centre
Local knowledge
Current and forecast weather conditions
Time of day
Potential community exposure and impacts
Potential infrastructure exposure and impacts
Consider issuing early Community Information/Warning
Fire Services jurisdiction
Potential water points
Columns of smoke and/or gas clouds

questions.q: Q118. Ensure the following principles are included in Size Up:
a: Facts – What do you know that is affecting the incident, mitigation, and safety?
Probabilities – What is likely to happen, including potential for fire spread and risk to life?
Own situation – Do you have sufficient resources and capabilities? Should you respond more?
Decision – What is your objective for the incident?
Plan – How do you plan to resolve the incident, and what strategies and tactics will be applied?

questions.q: Q119. On-scene emergency services should liaise with any on-site representatives, occupants, technicians, or witnesses to gather what information:
a: Nature of premises/occupancy status
Risk to life and evacuation status
Fuel types and fuel loads
Potential exposures
Known hazards
Access/egress paths
On-site intelligence (property plans, Emergency Information book/manifest)

questions.q: Q120. Utilise B-SAHF during Size Up at a structure fire:
a: Building – construction style/materials that impact fire behaviour
Smoke – volume, velocity, density, and colour
Air track – inlets and outlets, what is the building ventilation profile?
Heat – blackening/crazing of windows, blistering of paintwork
Flame – colour (yellow/red/blue), indicator of oxygen supply to fire

questions.q: Q121. Use the following format for all Strategic Level Situation Reports:
a: Incident type and status
Incident potential – risks to life and property
Loss and damage
Incident objective(s)
Likely resource requirements and commitment
Community warnings issued

questions.q: Q122. Consider sending a Strategic Level Situation Report in the following circumstances:
a: An emergency or priority situation such as Mayday or loss of PAR
Upon request from the Communications Centre
Changes to the IAP
Significant community evacuations or impacts

questions.q: Q123. Use the CAN format for all Tactical Level Situation Reports:
a: Conditions – What are the current conditions of the incident/task?
Actions – What actions are being implemented?
Needs – What additional resources are required?

questions.q: Q124. Consider sending a Tactical Level Situation Report in the following circumstances:
a: Upon request from the chain of command
Periodically while undertaking a task
New critical information is discovered
Assigned tasks are completed or unable to be completed
When further resources are required or no longer required

questions.q: Q125. What is the difference between a Situational and Tactical SitRep?
a: Strategic Level Situation Reports are to contain information relevant to the incident strategies and objective(s)
Tactical Level Situation Reports are to only contain information relevant to an assigned task and must be kept brief

questions.q: Q126. When to conduct a Personnel Accountability Report PAR?
a: Receipt of a mayday message
Use of emergency evacuation signal
A change from offensive to defensive strategies
Crews are failing to respond

questions.q: Q127. Ensure a PAR is requested only by the following authorised personnel for their area of accountability:
a: Incident Controller
Operations Officer
Safety Officer
Sector Commander
BA Entry Officer (BAEO)

questions.q: Q128. What Actions Should be Conducted After Unaccounted for resources on Request of PAR?
a: Continue to try and make contact with any unaccounted for appliances, resources, or personnel in the situation of a failed PAR
Send a nearby resource(s) to the last known location of any unaccounted for personnel to try and make contact
Issue a Mayday message if a resource remains unaccounted for
Utilise RIT to begin searching for unaccounted resources where appropriate

questions.q: Q129. How do you as an OIC Maintain Personnel Accountability?
a: Ensure Fast Cards are completed and accurately reflect appliance crews. This is the responsibility of the OIC of the appliance
Ensure all OICs of appliances report to the Incident Control Point for tasking upon arrival at an incident
Avoid splitting appliance crews where practicable. Appliances should be directed to complete a task as a unit where possible
Ensure personnel performing functional roles account for resources under their command

Maintain accountability when supervising a resource, team, or functional role. Ensure all radio calls to allocated call sign are answered, and immediately report any loss of personnel accountability as soon as possible

questions.q: Q130. When should a Red Flag Warning be issued?
a: Consider a Red Flag Warning when a change in circumstances presents a significant risk to Safety or is predicted to present a significant risk to safety:
Weather Conditions
Fuel Conditions
Incident/Fire Behaviour
Potential hazardous atmosphere
Equipment availability
Communications issues/difficulties
Access issues/difficulties
Structural collapse
LPG BLEVE or other possible explosion

questions.q: Q131. Who can Issue a Red Flag Warning?
a: Sector Commander
Division Commander
Operations Officer
Incident Controller

questions.q: Q132. What must be done once a Red Flag Warning is received?
a: Confirm the Red Flag Warning has been received
Repeat the key points of the warning back to the sender to demonstrate understanding
Notify all responding and support agency personnel of the Red Flag Warning under your supervision
Obtain a confirmation from these personnel that they have received the warning

questions.q: Q133. Convey Red Flag Warnings by any appropriate means, including:
a: Radio
Telephone
Written notice
Verbal

questions.q: Q134. Document/log all details of the Red Flag Warning, including:
a: Name of person who issued the Red Flag Warning
The time it was issued
The information it contained
How it was issued
Who it was issued to and who was informed (both up and down the chain of command)
The time acknowledgements were received from those you supervise

questions.q: Q135. When to transmit a MAYDAY?
questions.a: Transmit a mayday immediately when in a life-threatening situation, or when others are in a life-threatening situation.

questions.q: Q136. When should you not transmit a MAYDAY Message?
questions.a: Mayday Messages should not be transmitted during training scenarios.

questions.q: Q137. How to transmit a MAYDAY?
a: Mayday Mayday Mayday
Name of person transmitting or unit/call sign
Location
Situation Report / Assignment / Task
Resources / Assistance

questions.q: Q138. How to respond to a MAYDAY?
a: Confirm the details by the caller
Commit Resources to the intervention effort including any pre-determined RIT
Establish a rescue sector (as determined by the IC)
Allocate appropriate radio channels to the intervention effort
Issue a general message or a Red Flag Warning to the Fire/incident channels, if appropriate

questions.q: Q139. Ensure the following is completed once the Mayday situation has been resolved:
a: Notify Communications Centre
Notify all personnel on the fireground
Ensure any Duress Alarms activated have been reset
Resume prioritising the combating of the fire or incident

questions.q: Q140. Why issue a Red, Red, Red Priority Signal?
questions.a: To send an urgent message where extreme radio congestion exists, in order to gain priority access to Communications Centre and the fireground channel(s).

questions.q: Q141. Scenarios where a Red, Red, Red may be required include the following:
a: A word back message requiring the escalation of an incident
A general message communicating a significant fireground safety issue
A Red Flag Warning

questions.q: Q142. Detail when to transmit the Emergency Evacuation Signals:
a: Imminent Structural collapse
Bushfire burn over
Landslip
Uncontrolled release of gasses

questions.q: Q143. Activate an Emergency Evacuation Signal in the following sequence:
a: Three short blasts, each for one second duration
Wait ten seconds and repeat
Repeat this sequence until all persons are accounted for

questions.q: Q144. How may the Emergency Evacuation Signal warning be given?
a: Appliance/vehicle horn
Air horn
Evacuation Signal Unit (ESU)
Whistle
Loud hailer
PA system on appliance

questions.q: Q145. Complete the following Actions immediately upon hearing an Emergency Evacuation Signal:
a: Ensure all other crew members are aware of the signal
Report to immediate supervisor
Evacuate to a safe area

questions.q: Q146. Requirement to Wear Breathing Apparatus:
a: Don BA in a state of readiness at any alarm of fire, unless directed otherwise by the IC after completing a Size Up
Put on facemask and activate the BA when a Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) identifies that a confirmed or potential hazardous atmosphere may exist
Do not wait for an order from the Incident Controller to don and activate BA where it is obvious that a hazardous atmosphere exists
Ensure BA remains donned and activated at all times when a hazardous atmosphere exists. Only the IC/SC/OO can determine when BA is no longer required
Ensure P2 masks are not worn in situations where BA should be worn
Note: P2 masks only provide particulate protection (e.g., hazardous fibres such as asbestos)

questions.q: Q147. Breathing Apparatus crews entering the hazardous atmosphere (Hot Zone) should Consider:
a: Ensure BA is donned correctly
Do not commence initial entry into a hazardous atmosphere with a cylinder pressure less than 250 bar
Work in teams of at least two, where appropriate
Select the designated fireground channel on portable radios
Deposit BA tally tags at BA entry prior to entering a potential or confirmed hazardous atmosphere
Check time out/low-air periodically
Exit the fireground accompanied by at least one other member of the team when the cylinder pressure gauge of the BA reaches a pre-determined level, or the cylinder low-air warning signal operates
Proceed towards the sound of a full alarm or distress signal. Rendering assistance is to take precedence over the work at hand. Communicate the situation to IC/SC/OO
Withdraw immediately upon the operation of the evacuation alarm
Report to BA Entry and collect tally tags upon exiting the fire/incident
Report to BA Service (if one is in operation) after collecting BA tally tags from the BA Entry
Do not re-enter a hazardous atmosphere with a cylinder pressure of less than 200 bar unless a Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA) has been completed, and it has been deemed acceptable

questions.q: Q148. BA Stage 1 – Incident Controller Responsibilities and Actions:
a: Implement BA Stage 1 where it is necessary to use BA and monitor BA wearers at the incident, where the following circumstances exist:
BA operations are limited and not complex
The incident requires no more than one BA Entry Point
BA guidelines are not required
Ensure accountability of BA teams is managed through the use of a BA Control Board
Consider the following when establishing BA Stage 1 operations:
Allocate BA Teams, call signs and fireground channels, ensuring personnel are working in teams of at least two where appropriate
Avoid splitting appliance crews when establishing BA Teams wherever possible. This will assist in maintaining personnel accountability
Allocate call signs in line with appliance numbers (e.g., "Pumper 22 BA Team")
Ensure BA Teams are operating on the assigned fireground channel
Advise the Communications Centre that "BA Stage 1 is in operation". This can also be completed within the wordback
Establish a BA Entry Point as soon as possible and delegate the role of BA Entry Officer (BAEO) once resources become available. Until delegated, the IC is accountable for all BA operations
Establish a Rapid Intervention Team

Establish a DEBRiS Zone based on a Safe Person Approach, Dynamic Risk Assessment (DRA), taking into consideration the incident alarm level, extent of the contamination, and/or number of personnel to be processed

questions.q: Q149. BA Stage 1 – BA Entry Officer (BAEO) Responsibilities and Actions:
a: Record the following on the BA Control Board:
Names of personnel operating within the hazardous atmosphere (Hot Zone)
BA Team call sign(s) and location
Low air and time of whistle
Allocated fireground channel(s)
Track locations of BA Teams and record on BA Stage 1 Control Board. Consider utilising a mud map to assist with location accountability
Ensure all personnel exiting the hazardous atmosphere retrieve BA tally and proceed through DEBRiS, where established

questions.q: Q150. BA Stage 2 – Incident Controller responsibilities and actions:
a: Implement BA Stage 2 operations when a greater level of control is required to manage and monitor the safety of BA wearers in complex BA operations
Delegate the role of BA Control Officer (BACO) when enough resources are available on scene
Establish the appropriate number of BA Entry Points and allocate call signs for each (e.g., BA Entry Sector 1)
Ensure the appropriate Emergency Evacuation Signal device is established
Establish additional Rapid Intervention Teams to support each BA Entry Point, as required
Establish the appropriate number of BA Service Areas as per DEBRiS
Ensure a sufficient supply of BA equipment is provided to the incident by responding the appropriate resources to support this capability
Utilise personal or main guidelines in extreme conditions where practicable
